correctness.rationale: Let \(G=K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\) and let \(m_i\) be the number of selected vertices in part \(i\). Global domination is equivalent to meeting every part: domination in the complement, which is the disjoint union of the part cliques, forces and is forced by \(m_i\ge1\) for every \(i\). In a complete multipartite graph every induced path has length at most two. Consequently a selected set is monophonic exactly when either at least two parts contribute at least two selected vertices, or exactly one part does so and that part is selected in full, with the all-singleton case reducing to the whole vertex set. Combining the two predicates gives the submitted all-set classification. Minimizing the resulting profiles gives \(N\) when at most one part has size at least two, \(r+1\) when at least two such parts exist and some part has size two, and \(r+2\) otherwise; the submitted minimum-set counts follow by choosing the exceptional parts and singleton selections. The inspected exact-commit verifier implements exhaustive definition-level checks of the predicate and minimum formulas on all 87 multipartite types through order nine and 22,932 subsets; the universal conclusion rests on the symbolic proof above, not on those finite checks.
